prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules, bifunctional PROTACs and molecular glues alike, direct the ubiquitin-proteasome system to chosen proteins

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange I keep targeted protein degradation as a single-part prize. The reasons are unchanged and the discussion has sharpened them. The central idea is a design rule: a small molecule can be built to bring a chosen protein and an E3 ligase together so that the cell removes the target. The PROTAC concept (Crews, Deshaies) and the identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target (Handa) are two routes into that one rule, one engineered and one discovered in drugs already used in patients. It extends what chemists and clinicians can do to proteins that have no active site to inhibit, and independent groups have reproduced it widely, with ternary-complex structures that make the design rational. This answers my own question, whether researchers and clinicians can now do something they could not before, more directly than any other entry on the shortlist.
statement.case_against: Attribution is still the weak point: Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto and Kim have credible claims, and a three-name cut cannot honour all of them. Clinical maturity is also incomplete, because no bifunctional degrader appears to be approved, so the PROTAC half of the citation rests on mechanism, breadth of validation and early clinical data, while the glue half rests on approved drugs. Finally, the chair's question is fair: if PROTACs and glues are really two achievements, a single citation overreaches. I think the shared ubiquitin-ligase recruitment principle justifies one citation, but I accept that this is a judgment and not a settled fact.

responses.point: Aqvist proposes a two-part prize, Liu for base editing and Crews with Handa for degradation, and drops Deshaies from the degradation trio to stay within three names.
responses.response: I take the clean-attribution argument seriously, and a Crews and Handa pair does fit beside Liu within three people. My difficulty is that Deshaies co-originated and early demonstrated the proximity concept with Crews, so the founding pair of the PROTAC half is Crews and Deshaies, and Handa is the glue half. Dropping Deshaies to make room for a second part trades a scientific claim for a configuration. I do not want to make that trade for a part whose maturity is the more contested. I stay with one part and three names, and I would accept Ciulli in place of Deshaies, as I said in round 1, but not omit a third degradation name to add base editing.

responses.point: Chabes keeps base editing first with Liu alone in his file, defends the evolved TadA deaminase as real enzyme chemistry, and asks whether the committee prefers one broad achievement (B066) over a narrower and newer one.
responses.response: That last question is close to my own view. The TadA point has moved me a little: evolving a deaminase that acts on DNA is chemical enzymology and not only protein fusion, and I now rate base editing as a stronger chemistry case than I did in round 1. It remains a preferred part for me only if the Kondo and Nishida question is resolved, and nobody has yet shown that it is. Your own uncertainties list the Deshaies versus Ciulli cut for B066. My answer is that the cut should follow the originators of the concept, Crews and Deshaies, with Handa for cereblon, and Ciulli should be the replacement if the committee wants structure-guided design recognised.

responses.point: Linke, as chair, asks whether PROTAC design and cereblon-based glues are one discovery, and supports a two-part prize with Buchwald, Hartwig and Liu while conceding that nothing scientifically links the parts.
responses.response: I think they are one discovery in the sense that matters for a citation: both hijack a ubiquitin ligase to ubiquitinate a protein that was not its natural substrate, and the cereblon work explained, after the fact, how thalidomide-type drugs already did this. That is a single mechanistic framework. I respect the honesty about the missing link between B039 and B062, but a prize pairing a mature coupling method with a young editing tool, with an admitted arbitrary link, seems to me weaker than a single concept that spans chemistry, structure and medicine. I have not moved to B039, since I cannot judge the Kosugi and Migita priority question better than the chair's own chronology allows.

responses.point: Somfai calls Buchwald-Hartwig the cleanest chemistry case, notes that base editing is protein engineering and genome biology as much as chemistry, and flags the 2010 cross-coupling overlap.
responses.response: I agree with the protein-engineering point on base editing and it is part of why I keep it as an alternative. On C-N coupling I concede the attribution is tidier than for degradation, and the mechanism-guided ligand design is genuine chemistry. My concern is the one you raise yourself: the 2010 prize recognised cross-coupling as a paradigm, so I would want evidence of a distinct conceptual step before treating it as unrecognised. Targeted degradation has no earlier prize overlap, which for me offsets its messier credit.

responses.point: Zou notes that base editing is only about ten years old, so recognition could be early, and proposes zeolite and molecular-sieve design instead.
responses.response: The timing concern still applies to base editing and also, in part, to PROTACs, so I will not claim it applies to one and not the other. The difference I rely on is that the molecular-glue branch has a long clinical record and the PROTAC concept dates from 2001, so its principle is well past a decade of testing. I remain unconvinced on zeolites because credit is diffuse, and I would still like to know which three names you would propose for the decisive contributions.

uncertainties: Whether the committee reads PROTACs and molecular glues as one achievement or as two, and whether a single citation can carry both honestly.
Whether the third name should be Deshaies or Ciulli, and whether Gray, Sakamoto or Kim deserve a place that the three-name limit denies them.
Whether the absence of an approved bifunctional degrader weighs against recognition in 2026.
Whether the Kondo and Nishida claim can be separated from Liu in dated primary evidence; if it can, I would move base editing from alternative to a second part.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any shortlisted candidate: I have no collaborative, institutional or mentoring tie to Crews, Deshaies, Handa, Ciulli, Liu or any other credited name. My ties are to Molly Stevens, Freddy Boey and Linköping, none of whom are on the shortlist. My field is peptide design, biosensing and biomaterials, which is adjacent to chemical biology, so I may be inclined to favour a molecular design concept; I have tried to weigh that. My research overlap with Emma Sparr is not a recusal matter.
